notes: Pedestrian and bicycle counts are not available: the delivered CRIS exports have no pedestrian or bicycle field.
run_off_road counts all single-vehicle crashes (CRIS manner of collision 'one motor vehicle'); it is a proxy, not a roadway-departure flag.
head_on = opposite direction, both going straight; left_turn_opposing = opposite direction with a left-turning vehicle (not head-on).
night = dark lighted, dark not lighted or dark unknown lighting; wet = wet or standing water.

evidence.study_reference: Le et al., 2017; Safety Effects of Low-Cost Systemic Safety Improvements at Signalized and Stop-Controlled Intersections
evidence.limitations: Empirical Bayes before-after, South Carolina; 434 sites. Applies to the package, not one sign or marking by itself.

Check treatment prerequisites, geometry, traffic volumes, and existing equipment: Four-leg stop-controlled roadway intersection on two-lane roads. Major-road ADT 250-42520; minor-road ADT 90-13270. Standard and actuated beacons were studied; confirm the chosen installation.
Complete source verification; current status: evidence_checked_indexed

evidence.study_reference: Srinivasan et al., 2008; Safety Evaluation of Flashing Beacons at Stop Controlled Intersections
evidence.limitations: Empirical Bayes study. Adjusted SE 0.04. HSM explicitly recommends caution because uncertainty includes no effect or an increase. Aggregate scope; not an angle-only estimate. Not an RRFB pedestrian-crossing treatment.

sections.crash_profile: From {{window_start}} to {{window_end}}, {{total_3y}} crashes occurred at this unsignalized intersection, with {{ka_3y}} fatal or suspected serious injury crashes and {{kabc_3y}} suspected minor or possible injury crashes. The most frequent crash types were angle and rear-end ({{angle_3y}} and {{rear_end_3y}}), with some run-off-road and left-turn-opposing incidents. Pedestrian and bicycle counts are not available.
sections.why_flagged: The site is flagged for inclusion in the high-injury network, a relatively high injury crash rate ({{fsi_rate}} per mile), and substantial traffic exposure ({{aadt}} vehicles/day). It ranks {{rank_city_actionable}} among actionable city sites. Recent crashes on nearby sites also contribute to its risk profile.

countermeasures.rationale: This systemic signing and marking improvement package is supported by broader evidence for all crash types and injury severities per {{cmf:8867}}. The entry is not a direct crash-type match and requires engineering review to confirm prerequisites and applicability.

Flashing beacons at stop-controlled intersections are supported by broader evidence for all crash types and severities per {{cmf:446}}. This entry is not a direct crash-type match and requires engineering review for geometry, traffic volumes, and installation details.

sections.benefit_cost: A benefit could not be computed for either countermeasure. The CMF entries do not support a numerical benefit calculation due to severity scope differences and lack of planning-level unit cost or service life data.
sections.next_steps: Conduct an engineering review to assess site geometry, traffic volumes, and existing equipment for both treatments. Confirm whether prerequisites for signing/marking improvements and flashing beacons are met. Review recent crash patterns for further insight and coordinate with TxDOT as needed.
